mission: Tess clears the board. From his anonymous Greyline office, he determines Korda has become too visible and orders Korda's elimination. The killing is shaped as a public fall-guy narrative: rogue security director, illegal contractors, no institutional culpability for the Foundation. Tess does not gloat. He treats the death as logistics — 'Korda was becoming visible. This cleans the board.' He then orders the Iresh operation accelerated, specifically because Ben Skywalker and Talon Veyr are now actively involved. The acceleration is not a panic move; it is a calculated adjustment to the threat profile.
why_now: Korda's near-capture at the transfer node made him a thread anyone could pull. Tess's discipline is exactly this: remove the thread before it is pulled, reshape the story before anyone else writes it, and move the real operation faster than the investigation chasing it.
conflict: Tess against exposure. Every move that protects the Vigil costs him an asset or a margin: killing Korda buys silence at the price of attention, accelerating Iresh buys time at the price of field risk. He pays both without hesitation — and that is what should frighten the reader.
turning_point: Tess orders Korda's elimination and accelerates the Iresh operation — the board is cleared, the clock shortened.
closing_hook: Korda's file closes on Tess's desk display. The Iresh timetable advances. Somewhere below, the city is about to learn the official story.
setting: A Greyline Strategic Services secure office on the forty-second floor of a mid-tier Coruscant commercial tower: sleek, clean, anonymous. Durasteel desk, single visitor chair, no personal effects. The skyline through the viewport is the city that voted the Jedi out — Tess finds that neither ironic nor interesting.
emotional_trajectory: Tess should feel terrifying because he is calm and operational. He does not rage, he does not gloat, he just clears the board. The cache raid should land through absence rather than action — Ben and Talon walk into a destroyed space, no enemy present, only the evidence of professionalism. The frame should make Talon go cold, not hot. The Luke call should be the quietest beat in the chapter, and the most painful. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: Plain-language consequence: the bad guys just closed every option Ben had except the most dangerous one. They did it surgically. They did it because Ben is involved. The clock is no longer theoretical. Craft notes: - The cache raid happens off-screen for Ben. He arrives after. The reader experiences the loss through the destroyed space. - Who told Greyline where the cache was stays unanswered. The drafter should plant the question without resolving it. - Tess’s tradecraft fingerprint on the frame should be quiet, not declamatory. Talon notices, gives one small reaction, names it in a sentence when Ben asks.

stakes.personal: Ben walks into the burned cache and sees the ash where the documentary reconstruction was. Whatever case he was building for Saba is gone. He is no longer in the position of a Jedi Knight making a careful institutional argument — he is hunted, legally compromised, and out of official options.
stakes.interpersonal: The Talon frame is Tess's tradecraft fingerprint: specific construction patterns, a particular routing of planted evidence. Talon recognizes it in one sentence and goes cold. The valve doesn't shut — it freezes. Tess knows exactly how Talon thinks. That's the worst part. The second Luke call from the apartment is short, quiet, and ends without resolution — Luke understands what Ben has decided and doesn't try to stop him.
stakes.external: Three beats compound: (1) Korda is dead, shaped as a fall-guy narrative — rogue security director, no Foundation culpability. (2) The cache is professionally destroyed — no documentary case survives. (3) Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime — Luke's quiet legal cover is ended. Simultaneously, Greyline's Iresh staging has accelerated past the timeline Ben captured from Korda. Every door is closed except the most dangerous one.

sensory_details: Tess's office: durasteel desk, single visitor chair, no personal effects, forty-second floor — the view from here is other buildings' climate exhaust. Clean and anonymous, the kind of space designed to carry no forensic weight. Iressa's cache after the raid: slagged terminals, ash where her labeled crates of datachips were, the smell of burning plastoid that hasn't fully cleared. The Skywalker apartment at night: familiar recycled air, the family holo still on the shelf — the same room, very different weight now.
canon_elements_needed: Shedu Maad / Hapes Jedi HQ continuity
Iresh physical geography and local survival rules

turning_point_detail.trigger: The report on Korda's blown cover crosses Tess's desk and meets a decision that was already made — visibility is the one failure Tess does not manage, only removes.
turning_point_detail.shift: The Vigil shifts from concealment to acceleration: with Skywalker active, the value of patience is gone, and Tess re-prices the whole operation in a sentence.
turning_point_detail.cost: Korda dies as a logistics line. The fall-guy narrative will hold — and the reader now knows the Foundation scandal Ben is chasing was authored, not uncovered.

emotional_arc.start: Tess POV: operational calm. No gloating, no anger — a man maintaining a system that failed once and will not fail the same way twice.
emotional_arc.shift: The 'Move her first' discipline under the surface: one flicker of the corridor logic that built him, visible only in how cleanly he orders a colleague's death.
emotional_arc.end: The board is clean. Tess turns to the Iresh acceleration with the same unhurried attention — and the chapter's dread is set: this man does not escalate; he adjusts.

key_beats.beat_description: From Tess's POV: Korda's elimination is ordered as a logistics problem; the public fall-guy narrative is shaped; the Iresh operation is accelerated because Ben Skywalker's involvement has moved the threat profile.
key_beats.state_change: The antagonist's response to Ben's investigation is calibrated and immediate — Korda was the loose variable, and Tess has removed him cleanly.
key_beats.pov_reaction: N/A — Tess POV; Tess experiences this as sorted logistics, no emotional register beyond operational confirmation.

key_beats.beat_description: The fall-guy narrative is shaped line by line: rogue security director, illegal contractors, no institutional culpability — the public story authored before the body is found.
key_beats.state_change: The Foundation's survival is decoupled from Korda's; the scandal now has an official shape that ends at a dead man.
key_beats.pov_reaction: professional satisfaction kept strictly proportional — a narrative is a tool, and Tess files it like one

key_beats.beat_description: Tess orders the Iresh operation accelerated because Ben Skywalker and Talon Veyr are actively involved — a calculated adjustment to the threat profile, not a panic move.
key_beats.state_change: The story's clock shortens: whatever Ben decides next, the expedition is already moving faster than his options.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the quiet arithmetic of a commander re-pricing risk — Skywalker is a variable, and variables get budgeted, not feared
